eye.because: W is the earliest: A's ground floor still has its two windows, and B has narrow two-pane windows with surrounds. In Y, Z and X the left windows of A are replaced by a shopfront with a fascia board and a blank panel, and B has wider three-pane windows. Y has D's gable windows glazed, as in W. In Z and X they are boarded, and a railing appears at A's left edge. Board-joint patterns on D's siding drift steadily W, Y, Z, X. I read the shopfront and widened windows as later changes, not a restoration; that is the main risk to the whole order. Z before X is less sure. Years are priors only: nothing in the images dates them absolutely. (My environment also carried the project's own notes; I did not use them to date anything.)

street.because: Two states show. In Z and Y, C's side windows are boarded and D's gable window is glazed. In X and W, C is glazed and D is boarded and shuttered. Matching the eye view, the first state comes earlier: D is glazed in the early eye frames and boarded in the late ones. D's siding joint pattern changes most between Z and the rest, Y and X are nearly identical, and W is the furthest from Z. The step from Y to X is the big swap of which house is boarded. X before W is the less sure part.

12m.because: In X and W, C's gable windows are boarded and D's are glazed (the early state). In Y and Z, C is glazed and D is boarded (the later state). D's siding joint pattern is identical in W and Y, so they sit either side of the swap. X is the most different from the others and Z is on the far side, which puts X first and Z last. The order inside each pair rests on that pattern only, so it is less sure than the split between the pairs.

city.because: X has A without the ground-floor shopfront and B with the old narrow windows, so it is earliest. Z has the shopfront and B's new wider windows, but still no railing at A's corner, with C boarded and D glazed. Y and W have the railing, C glazed, D boarded, and a boarded window on a house at the lower middle. W alone lacks an extra door on the wall of the house near E, which I read as the last change, so W is latest. Y versus W is the least certain pair, resting on that one door.
